caption_hook: Arizona has been a mountain range, a sea, a Sahara and a forest, all stacked in one canyon.

layers.name: SAN FRANCISCO PEAKS
layers.hook: A volcano taller than any in Arizona
layers.what: A volcanic field around Flagstaff has erupted for about 6 million years. The largest volcano, built from lava and ash, was about 16,000 ft before it collapsed.
layers.bonus: Humphreys Peak, its remnant, is Arizona's highest point at 12,633 ft.

layers.name: CHINLE FORMATION
layers.what: Rivers once carried logs and ash across this floodplain. Buried logs were replaced by quartz and other minerals, and erosion now exposes the colorful, banded badlands.
layers.bonus: The Painted Desert gets its pastel stripes from this layer's clay.

layers.name: KAIBAB LIMESTONE
layers.what: A warm shallow sea left this pale, cliff-forming limestone. It is full of sponges, shells and other sea life, and it forms the top of the Grand Canyon.
layers.bonus: Seashells sit on the rim at over 7,000 feet above sea level.

layers.name: REDWALL LIMESTONE
layers.what: This thick, hard limestone formed in a clear tropical sea. It stands as a sheer cliff roughly 500 feet high, stained red by iron washing down from the layers above.
layers.bonus: The red is only a stain: a fresh break shows gray rock underneath.

layers.name: TAPEATS SANDSTONE
layers.hook: Beach sand from the first big sea
layers.what: A rising Cambrian sea flooded the land and left a blanket of beach sand. It rests directly on far older rock, with well over a billion years missing in between.
layers.bonus: That gap is the Great Unconformity, a name John Wesley Powell used here in 1869.

layers.name: VISHNU BASEMENT
layers.hook: Mountain roots at the canyon floor
layers.what: At the bottom of the Grand Canyon, dark Vishnu Schist and pink granite are the roots of an ancient mountain range. The Colorado River cuts through them in the Inner Gorge.
layers.bonus: These rocks are about 40 percent as old as the Earth itself.
